title: Skincare Spa and Clinic Management
desc: Plan and run a small skincare spa or clinic: services, hygiene, consent, scheduling, products, pricing and client care.
outcomes: Explain service menus, scope of practice and hygiene rules.
Run client intake, consent and patch-test steps.
Build a schedule and cost per treatment.
Judge product claims and ingredient labels.
Launch a 30-day pilot with a client-care review.
task: Plan and pilot a small skincare spa service menu with hygiene plan, consent forms, pricing, schedule and client feedback log.
condition: A practice room or real licensed space, a spreadsheet, two peers and a licensed practitioner as mentor. Medical treatments are outside scope.
standard: Hygiene checklist passes; every service has a scope note; costs and price are shown; consent and patch-test steps are recorded; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Beauty therapists, spa owners, front-desk staff, small clinic managers.
evidence: service menu, hygiene plan, intake and consent forms, price sheet, pilot log
modules: Service menu and scope
Understand
Offer only what staff are trained and licensed to do.
Cleansing, facials, light exfoliation; leave medical treatments to doctors.
Write who can perform each service.
Refer skin concerns to a doctor.
The spa lists facials but refers a changing mole to a doctor.
Write a menu with scope notes.
Each service has a qualification need.
Hygiene and infection control
Apply
Clean spaces protect clients.
Hand washing, clean towels, single-use items, tool sterilising.
Surface cleaning between clients; waste handling.
Daily and weekly log.
A tool tray is sterilised for the full cycle and logged.
Write a hygiene checklist and a log.
All steps have a time and initials.
Client intake, consent, patch tests
Apply
Know the client before touching skin.
Ask about allergies, medicines, pregnancy, skin conditions.
Do patch tests 24 to 48 hours before new products where advised.
Written consent before treatment.
A client with a nut allergy avoids a nut-oil product.
Design an intake form.
Form covers allergy, medicine, consent.
Products and ingredients
Evaluate
Do not trust claims blindly.
Read ingredient lists; know common allergens.
Reject miracle claims; use claims the maker can support.
Store products at the right temperature and note expiry.
A cream lists fragrance as the first ingredient; the practitioner avoids it for sensitive skin.
Review 3 product labels.
Each review has a safety note.
Scheduling and capacity
Analyse
Time is the main resource.
Service time plus cleaning plus buffer.
Rooms and staff per slot.
Online booking and reminders.
A 60-minute facial uses 80 minutes of room time.
Build a day schedule for two staff.
No overlaps.
Pricing and profit
Evaluate
Know costs per treatment.
Staff time, products, rent share, laundry, booking fees.
Price to cover cost and margin.
Packages and loyalty must still be profitable.
Cost 520 INR; price 1,100 INR; margin 580 INR.
Cost 5 services.
Totals correct; currency shown.
Client care and complaints
Apply
Calm service wins trust.
Greet, explain, check comfort, aftercare tips.
Handle reactions: stop, rinse, record, advise a doctor if needed.
Review feedback weekly.
A client reports redness; staff stop, cool the skin, record and call the mentor.
Write a reaction protocol.
Steps in order with contact numbers.
Pilot and improve
Create
Run 30 days of service.
Track bookings, rebookings, complaints, product waste.
Fix top 3 issues.
Plan responsible disposal and fair pay.
Rebooking rises from 32% to 45% after aftercare cards.
Present the pilot review.
Numbers are real; three fixes dated.
quiz: To keep to training and licence.
A small test on skin before a full treatment.
What to do on a reaction?
Stop, rinse, record, get medical help if needed.
What costs go into a price?
Staff, products, rent share, laundry, fees.
What do you track in a pilot?
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others

ladder: L1: learner can name basic skin-care steps.
L2: learner knows hygiene and scope rules.
L3: learner can run intake and consent.
L4: learner can run a full client visit.
L5: learner can cost and price services.
L6: learner can lead a small spa team.
L7: learner can audit a spa for hygiene and fairness.
